title: contracts/architecture.json
description: App-owned architecture facts read by the architecture-and-boundaries checkers. Paths are repo-relative globs; {srcDir}, {servicesDir}, {dataDir}, {scriptsDir} and the other layout keys are filled from rn-skills.config.json or the defaults.

srcFolders.description: Top-level src/ folders beyond the canonical set (app, features, ui, theme, core, services, stores, data, api, i18n, config, hooks, canvas, games); each is a shared layer.

sdkPackagePatterns.description: Package names or name globs that also count as SDKs, added to the defaults (expo-*, react-native-*, *-react-native, *-react-native-*, @react-native-*/*, @*/react-native, @*/react-native-*, @*/*-react-native, @*/*-react-native-*). Runtime code may import such a package only once it is in vendorSdks or portlessSdks. When node_modules exists, a package that ships native code counts too.

vendorSdks.description: SDK package name -> the port that wraps it. Only adapter files may import it (subpaths count). null drops a default entry. Mirror each entry in eslint.config.mjs VENDOR_SDK_PATHS.

vendorSdkFiles.description: SDK package name -> the only adapter file globs that may import it. null drops a default entry.

portlessSdks.description: SDK package name -> why it needs no port (UI building blocks, read-only facts). Any file may import it. Every SDK the app's runtime code imports (a name matching sdkPackagePatterns, or a package that ships native code) is in vendorSdks or here. null drops a default entry.

bannedPackages.description: Package name -> what to use instead: architecture bans (a port or an API replaced the package). The checker also bans every doNotAdd package of contracts/dependency-policy.json (dependency-management), so keep install bans there. null drops a default entry.

adapterFiles.description: Extra adapter globs (defaults: {servicesDir}/*/*-adapter.ts, {dataDir}/**/*-adapter.ts, {dataDir}/**/*-sql-driver.ts, {dataDir}/**/*-save-store.ts, each with its .ios/.android/.native/.web platform files).

compositionRoot.description: Extra composition-root globs: files that may import adapters (defaults: services-context.tsx, create-device-services.ts, create-test-services.ts in {servicesDir}, and the data opener {dataDir}/open-device-*.ts). A file listed here may also import create-device-services (a startup module the root layout calls, or the App component of a React Navigation app).

nodeWorldFiles.description: Extra files that run in Node (defaults: app.config.ts, plugins/**, {scriptsDir}/**). App code never imports them.

serverFiles.description: Extra server files (globs outside the routes folder), such as src/server/** for helpers the API routes share. Defaults: every +api file under the routes folder and the root +middleware file. Server code may use Node built-ins and imports src/core, src/api, src/config, src/data, port types, expo-server and expo-router/server; the app never imports it.

allowedImports.description: Reasoned exceptions to the zone rules (feature-to-feature, layer-direction, ui-presentational, route-thin, core-pure, game-to-game, game-facing, and server-boundary for server code importing app code).

nonFeatureScreens.description: Screen files (*-screen.tsx) allowed outside src/features/, such as an error-boundary fallback.

testOnlyFolders.description: Folders reached only through the test-only entry; their files may keep a debug port and fake side by side and may import fakes.

importTimeExempt.description: Files allowed to do work at import time (polyfill installers).

gameFacing.description: Extra files every game (src/games/<game>/ outside rules/ and levels/) may import: the seam the game host defines (defaults: {coreDir}/**, {uiDir}/**, {themeDir}/**, {i18nDir}/**, {srcDir}/canvas/** (the canvas kit), {servicesDir}/*/*-port.ts).

assetExtensions.description: File extensions (without the dot) the app added to metro.config.js resolver.assetExts, added to the defaults (Metro's and Expo's asset extensions plus woff, woff2, lottie, riv). require() of such a file is an asset, not code.

packages.description: When multi-package: every folder under packages/, with its world, and every Node backend workspace outside packages/ (Cloud Functions in functions/) with its dir and world "node".

dir.description: The workspace folder, repo-relative and ending in name (default packages/<name>). Outside packages/ ("functions") it is a Node backend: deployed on its own, imported by nothing, so world must be "node"; its folder is listed in package.json workspaces.

pure.description: No framework packages; imports only itself and other pure packages.

world.description: node: tooling; nothing in the app imports it.
